title: An overview of Pulumi, CloudFormation, AWS CDK and OpenTofu

videos.script: Ana's network has been a Terraform configuration for sixteen lessons. It is not the only way to write it, and this lesson meets four others. {{tools}} The first is OpenTofu, which began as Terraform's own code. It split off in 2023, when Terraform's licence changed. Ana runs lesson 2's network through it, and the first command fails. {{fork}} The reason is one line, the address of the AWS provider. Each program fills in a different registry, and the lab only has one of them. {{registry}} Then CloudFormation, which is AWS's own service. You hand it a template, and AWS keeps the state for you, in a stack. {{stack}} The AWS CDK writes that template from a program. Ten lines of JavaScript become twenty-four resources, and two of them are NAT gateways, billed by the hour. {{synth}} Pulumi is a program too, with an engine and a state of its own. The lab cannot install it, so you will read its code without running it. {{pulumi}} By the end you will know what each tool changes in the model you already have, and what it costs to switch. {{compare}}
